summary: There is no pre2 scene at all. src/scenes/index.js:24 registers './07_pre2.js' but that file does not exist (it is the harmless '[page] 404' in the exporter log), so index.js:41 plus kit.js:88-97 substitute ONE fallback shot, `todo-pre2`, for the whole 14.77 s (32 beats, 8 bars). What the frames really show from 88.96 to 103.73 is a single locked-off wide view of the chat client in the warm palette: sidebar, header 'Love, explained geometrically' / online, an otherwise empty thread into which lines 56-63 are typed one under another as eight identical ~34 px orange serif message rows, and an idle composer. No cut, no camera move, no cursor, no settings drawer, no graphic, no character art, no reaction to any drum hit, and no transition at the 'trance' line. The plan that was never built (PLAN.md section 6 row 7; chat_script.json section 7) was the settings drawer again, 'faster and more invasive', with five rows - Gender F/M, Can say no, On call AM/PM, Role S/M, Loop - and the interface starting to ghost and double. Musically this is NOT a copy of pre1: same melody and the same four 2-bar phrases, but pre1's kick-on-every-beat is gone, replaced by ten isolated full-scale hits (mostly on off-beats) and then a 3.4 s drum-less break under the 'trance' line before the chorus downbeat at 103.73.

diagnosis: The director's note treats this stretch as 'like the first pre-chorus, but give it concrete graphics', i.e. as something to refine. The frames show there is nothing to refine: 88.96-103.73 is the engine's placeholder. For 14.77 s the picture is one unmoving chat window in which eight small orange lines appear in a column; the right half of the frame and most of the thread stay empty; the last 1.45 s is a literal freeze frame. It is 5.7x the film's average shot length (2.58 s) and, together with todo-alone, the purest instance of the director's general complaint (1) 'the whole film stays inside the chat UI and is monotonous'. Every specific wish in the feedback points at something that is simply absent: (a) [lyric] has no figure - neither the old art nor the new busts are loaded (art.js ART_NAMES lists only the six anime illustrations); (b) [lyric], [lyric] and the 'trance' are glyphs inside 34 px message rows, typed linearly by lyrics.typed() so each is on screen 0.3-0.7 s BEFORE it is sung, and none lands on a drum hit; (c) the user is missing - no cursor, no clicks, no drawer - so the story beat 'the user flips its settings again, more invasively' (PLAN.md row 7, chat_script section 7) is not told, and the later image in 10_error.js (the ten rows 'as the user left them') has no set-up; (d) there is no escalation over pre1, there is a collapse: pre1 is four fully designed 2-bar shots (drawer, macro + mosaic, full-width timeline band, centred sheet with a camera fly-out), pre2 is a text list. The fallback also breaks continuity at both ends: at 88.96 the sidebar pops back (v2-god and all of pre1 are side:0 layouts), the thread is empty, the highlighted sidebar row ('Are you always here') is not the open conversation, and the cursor that v2-god deliberately walks to the header's top-right corner during its last 0.36 s vanishes; at 103.73 a frozen wide view hard-cuts to a 1.85x close-up of the thread foot with only a faint flash. One assumption in the feedback needs correcting for the designer: pre2 is not rhythmically the same as pre1. pre1 has a kick on every beat, so its clicks sit on integer beats; pre2 has ten isolated heavy hits (91.05, 91.98, 94.93, 95.63, 96.31, 97.50, 97.97, 99.35, 100.04, 100.28), seven of them on off-beats, and then no drums at all from 100.5 to 103.7 while the 'trance' line is sung twice. Those hits bracket the phrase-ending nouns (the gender-M sits on/after 91.05 and ends at 91.98; PM sits between 94.93 and 95.63; the role-M ends on 99.35), which is what the director hears as 'the strong drum hit of the last noun of each phrase'; the fourth noun ('trance') has no hit at all, which is exactly why the director asks for a transition there instead. What is 'strong' here is therefore not anything on screen but the inherited system: the approved warm chat-client look, the pre1 interaction grammar, the written row copy, clean grid cut points at both ends, and a piece of music that hands the designer ten punctuation marks and a ready-made 3.4 s runway into the chorus.
keep: The approved look of the frame itself: warm palette state ('warm', config.json palettes), matte charcoal client, orange serif = the AI, cream = the user, sans = interface; no red and no grey may appear here (colour = state; this section is still 'warm').

The pre1 grammar as the thing to mirror and then escalate (04_pre1.js): four 2-bar shots; every cut lands on a user action; the cream cursor is the protagonist (ghost trail + click burst, cur() 93-98); the AI's lyric is the orange annotation under the row being touched (hint()/say()); a control can break out of the drawer and take the whole frame (band(), sheet()); giant serif-900 tokens for the two poles of a setting (the 204 px era tokens are the direct precedent for big F/M, AM/PM, S/M letters); the spark is the knob/the AI.

The written plan's five rows and their end states, because 10_error.js:36-37 and 253-260 later redraws them 'as the user left them': Gender = M, Can say no = off, On call = PM/full, Role = M, Loop = on (chat_script.json:846-852). Role is already specified as plain letters S / M on a segmented control, which matches the director's 'letters only, nothing subcultural' instruction.
